sourceText: Prioritize uninterrupted high-quality CPR, early epinephrine, oxygenation and ventilation, and rapid treatment of reversible causes.

sourceText: No definite central pulse detected within a pulse check of no more than 10 seconds.

sourceText: Hypovolemia, hypoxia, hydrogen ion excess/acidosis, hypo-/hyperkalemia, and hypothermia.

sourceText: Apply monitor/defibrillator pads. Treat asystole and PEA as nonshockable rhythms; do not defibrillate or perform transcutaneous pacing.

sourceText: If VF/pulseless VT develops, move to AC-09. If ROSC occurs, move to AC-10.

Do not treat a single automated blood-pressure value without considering the patient's complete perfusion assessment and BP trend.

reason: Perfusion-not-single-BP shock recognition retained.

sourceText: A normal mental status or GCS of 15 does not establish hemodynamic stability.

targets.text: A normal mental status or GCS of 15 does not exclude shock.

reason: Same normal mental status/GCS 15 not proof of hemodynamic stability retained.

sourceText: Obtain a 12-lead ECG when cardiac ischemia, dysrhythmia, pulmonary embolism, or cardiogenic shock is possible.

targets.text: Perform all EMT and AEMT actions; obtain and interpret a 12-lead ECG when cardiac ischemia, dysrhythmia, pulmonary embolism, or cardiogenic shock is possible.

reason: Exact ECG indications retained.

sourceText: Use waveform capnography when ventilation is assisted and when clinically useful in severe shock.

targets.text: Use waveform capnography when ventilation is assisted and when clinically useful for trending perfusion in severe shock.

reason: Same assisted-ventilation/severe-shock capnography indication retained.

sourceText: Follow Universal Patient Care, maintain the airway, support ventilation, provide oxygen when clinically indicated, prevent heat loss, and position according to the patient's condition.

targets.text: Follow Universal Patient Care; assess mental status, pulse quality, skin signs, capillary refill, blood-pressure trend, respiratory status, and evidence of inadequate perfusion.
Maintain the airway, assist ventilation when needed, and give oxygen for hypoxemia, respiratory distress, shock, or another clinical indication.
Position supine when tolerated unless respiratory distress, pulmonary edema, pregnancy, or another condition requires alternate positioning.
Prevent heat loss, obtain frequent vital signs, identify time-critical causes, and begin rapid transport with early receiving-facility notification.

reason: Universal care, airway/ventilation/indicated oxygen, condition-specific positioning and heat-loss prevention retained.

sourceText: Use 250 mL aliquots with reassessment in heart failure, renal failure, liver failure, suspected cardiogenic shock, or another condition with increased risk of volume overload.

targets.text: For heart failure, renal failure, liver failure, suspected cardiogenic shock, or another risk of volume overload, use 250 mL aliquots with reassessment after each aliquot.

reason: Same 250 mL high-risk group list and each-aliquot reassessment retained.

sourceText: For hemorrhagic shock without suspected traumatic brain injury when blood is unavailable, titrate warmed isotonic crystalloid only to maintain a palpable radial pulse, adequate mental status, or SBP approximately 80–90 mmHg; avoid unnecessary large-volume crystalloid. Control bleeding, reassess after treatment, and expedite definitive care.

targets.text: For suspected hemorrhagic shock without traumatic brain injury when blood is unavailable, titrate warmed isotonic crystalloid only to maintain a palpable radial pulse, adequate mental status, or SBP approximately 80–90 mmHg; avoid unnecessary large-volume crystalloid. Reassess after treatment.
Control external hemorrhage immediately using direct pressure, wound packing, tourniquets, pelvic stabilization, and other approved measures when indicated.
Prevent heat loss, obtain frequent vital signs, identify time-critical causes, and begin rapid transport with early receiving-facility notification.

reason: Same non-TBI hemorrhage/blood-unavailable warmed-fluid perfusion endpoints and volume avoidance, bleeding control and expedited transport retained.

sourceText: For suspected TBI, prevent hypotension and target adult SBP at least 110 mmHg, including age 70. Do not use permissive hypotension. Avoid hypoxemia and excessive crystalloid; use normal saline when crystalloid is required. Reassess blood pressure frequently and after treatment.

targets.text: Prevent hypotension: target adult SBP at least 110 mmHg, including age 70. Do not use permissive hypotension. Avoid hypoxemia and excessive crystalloid; use normal saline when crystalloid is required. Reassess blood pressure frequently and after treatment.

reason: Exact TBI adult target including age 70, no permissive hypotension, normal-saline/oxygenation/crystalloid cautions and reassessment retained.

sourceText: For persistent hypotension or inadequate perfusion after an appropriate fluid trial—or earlier when additional fluid is contraindicated—begin a Paramedic vasopressor infusion with continuous ECG and frequent blood-pressure monitoring.

targets.text: For persistent hypotension or inadequate perfusion after an appropriate fluid trial—or earlier when further fluid is contraindicated—begin norepinephrine 0.05–0.5 mcg/kg/min IV/IO and titrate to adequate perfusion and MAP at least 65 mmHg.
Use continuous ECG monitoring and frequent blood-pressure reassessment during vasopressor treatment.

reason: Same persistent-shock or fluid-contraindicated trigger and continuous ECG/frequent BP monitoring retained.

sourceText: Use epinephrine infusion 2–10 mcg/min IV/IO when norepinephrine is unavailable or significant bradycardia accompanies shock; titrate to adequate perfusion and MAP at least 65 mmHg.

targets.text: When norepinephrine is unavailable or significant bradycardia accompanies shock, begin epinephrine infusion 2–10 mcg/min IV/IO and titrate to adequate perfusion and MAP at least 65 mmHg.

reason: Exact norepinephrine-unavailable/bradycardia epinephrine alternative, full dose/route/target retained.

sourceText: Do not use indiscriminate large-volume crystalloid in uncontrolled hemorrhage, pulmonary edema, cardiogenic shock, or suspected volume overload.

targets.text: Do not give indiscriminate large-volume crystalloid in uncontrolled hemorrhage, pulmonary edema, cardiogenic shock, or suspected volume overload.

reason: Exact indiscriminate large-volume crystalloid prohibition retained.

sourceText: Do not use permissive hypotension when traumatic brain injury is suspected.

targets.text: Do not use permissive hypotension when traumatic brain injury is suspected.

reason: Exact no permissive hypotension for suspected TBI retained.

sourceText: Do not delay transport for repeated peripheral-IV attempts, completion of a fluid target, or normalization of blood pressure.

targets.text: Begin transport early, notify the receiving facility, and do not delay for repeated IV attempts, completion of a fluid target, or normalization of blood pressure.

reason: Exact repeated-IV/fluid-target/BP-normalization transport-delay safeguards retained.

sourceText: Beyond approximately 20 weeks, use left uterine displacement or left lateral positioning when feasible and follow AO-03 for pregnancy-related causes.

targets.text: For pregnancy beyond approximately 20 weeks, use left uterine displacement or left lateral positioning when feasible, avoid prolonged supine positioning, treat hemorrhage or another cause, and follow AO-03.

reason: Same >approximately 20-week uterine-displacement/lateral positioning and AO-03 pathway retained.

sourceText: Interfacility transfer after hospital-administered Tenecteplase (TNK) for suspected acute ischemic stroke.

targets.text: Interfacility transfer after hospital-administered Tenecteplase (TNK) for suspected acute ischemic stroke.

reason: Exact transfer-population duplicate.

sourceText: Continue only an antihypertensive infusion specifically ordered by the sending facility and accepted under the interfacility-transfer policy; titrate only to written parameters.

targets.text: Continue an antihypertensive infusion only under written sending-facility orders and accepted pump parameters. Do not initiate or titrate a new antihypertensive under AM-06 without Medical Control or receiving-facility direction.

reason: Same written-order/accepted-pump-parameter limitation and no new treatment/titration without direction retained.

sourceText: Avoid unnecessary invasive procedures and IM medications. Apply prolonged direct pressure after any essential vascular access.

targets.text: Assist with authorized monitoring and essential vascular access. Avoid unnecessary invasive procedures, IM medication, and additional vascular attempts after thrombolysis.
Apply prolonged direct pressure after any necessary vascular access.

reason: Same unnecessary invasive/IM avoidance and prolonged access-site direct pressure retained.

sourceText: Begin immediately lifesaving care at the patient side when safe, then move promptly once critical interventions are underway.

targets.text: Treat airway, ventilation, severe hemorrhage, tension pneumothorax, hypoglycemia, anaphylaxis, dysrhythmia, and shock before prolonged movement when safe.
Move promptly once critical interventions are underway; plan reassessment stops during prolonged extrication and reassess at least every 5 minutes.

reason: Same safe immediate life-threat intervention before moving promptly once underway retained.

sourceText: GCS 15 does not equal stability.

targets.text: A normal GCS or initially acceptable BP does not exclude a crashing patient; reassess after every intervention.

reason: Same normal-GCS-not-stability caution retained.

sourceText: Use NIPPV only when the patient can protect the airway and is not vomiting or peri-arrest.

targets.text: Do not use NIPPV for vomiting, facial trauma, inability to cooperate, inability to protect the airway, or impending arrest.

reason: Same airway/vomiting/impending-arrest NIPPV restrictions retained with additional exclusions.

sourceText: Call for additional hands and advanced resources early.

targets.text: Position, suction, use BVM ventilation and oxygen when indicated, control hemorrhage, apply AED/monitor support, prevent heat loss, request resources early, and prepare transport.

reason: Same early additional-resource request retained.
